stories.headline: Alphabet Sells Record ¥576.5B ($3.6B) in Debut Yen Bond, the Biggest Ever by a Non-Japanese Issuer

key_facts.fact: Alphabet sold ¥576.5 billion ($3.6 billion) of yen-denominated bonds on May 15, the largest-ever yen deal by a non-Japanese company, breaking Berkshire Hathaway's 2019 record.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet Inc. sold ¥576.5 billion ($3.6 billion) of bonds in the biggest ever yen deal by a non-Japanese company as competition to fund centers and AI infrastructure intensifies.

key_facts.fact: The debut yen offering came in multiple tranches with maturities from 3 to 40 years and coupons between 1.965% and 4.599%; the five-year tranche of ¥200.5 billion priced at 50 bps over mid-swaps.
key_facts.excerpt: The debut yen bond by the parent of Google includes ¥200.5 billion of five-year bonds at 50 basis points over mid-swaps, according to people familiar with the matter. There were six other tranches.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet plans capital expenditures of up to $190 billion in 2026 to expand AI infrastructure and is broadening funding channels beyond US dollars after recent issuances in euros, sterling, Canadian dollars and Swiss francs.
key_facts.excerpt: Google parent company, Alphabet, has raised 576.5 billion yen ($3.6 billion) through its first-ever yen-denominated bond sale, marking the largest bond issuance in Japanese currency by a foreign company... The company has also flagged capital expenditure of up to $190 billion this year as it accelerates investment in AI-related infrastructure and services.

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes 2028 Policy Paper Urging US to Tighten Chip Controls and Curb Distillation to Hold AI Lead

key_facts.fact: In a new paper released May 14, Anthropic argues democracies can secure a commanding AI lead by 2028 if the US tightens controls on advanced compute to PRC labs, disrupts distillation of US models, and accelerates AI adoption among allies.
key_facts.excerpt: This scenario can be achieved if policymakers act now to tighten controls on advanced compute to PRC labs, disrupt their efforts to distill America's best AI models, and accelerate democracies' adoption of AI.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warns that without action the US faces a 'destabilizing neck-and-neck race with the CCP two years from now'.
key_facts.excerpt: In advancing these policies, we are hopeful that democracies can secure a commanding lead by 2028, and avoid a destabilizing neck-and-neck race with the CCP two years from now.

key_facts.fact: The paper says PRC labs benefit from access to export-controlled US chips via smuggling and foreign data centers, and that closing those loopholes would lower China's compute ceiling and impair distillation attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: PRC labs benefit from access to export-controlled American chips via smuggling and foreign data centers, and gaps in SME controls accelerate their self-sufficiency efforts. Tightening controls and ramping up enforcement budgets can help close these loopholes... a lower compute ceiling could also materially impair distillation attacks.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also calls on the Trump administration to 'champion the export of American AI', promoting global adoption of US-developed hardware and models to deny China footholds.
key_facts.excerpt: Champion the export of American AI. As public and commercial sectors around the world increasingly adopt AI, the Trump administration should continue its efforts to promote the global adoption of trusted AI hardware and models developed and shaped by democratic principles.

sources.title: 2028: Two scenarios for global AI leadership

stories.headline: Biogen Reports First Phase 2 Tau-Targeting ASO to Show Both Pathology Reduction and Cognitive Benefit in Early Alzheimer's

key_facts.fact: Biogen on May 14 announced topline Phase 2 CELIA results for diranersen (BIIB080), an antisense oligonucleotide targeting tau, in early Alzheimer's — the first randomized Phase 2 of a tau-directed therapy to show both biomarker impact and cognitive benefit.
key_facts.excerpt: Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB) today announced compelling topline results from the Phase 2 CELIA study evaluating diranersen (BIIB080), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy targeting tau, in individuals with early Alzheimer's disease. The CELIA results provide the first evidence from a randomized Phase 2 study of a tau-directed therapy demonstrating both robust biomarker impact and cognitive benefit in early Alzheimer's disease.

key_facts.fact: The primary endpoint of CELIA was the assessment of dose change from baseline on the Clinical Dementia Rating; secondary and exploratory endpoints included CSF tau biomarkers and tau PET imaging.
key_facts.excerpt: The primary endpoint of CELIA was assessment of dose [change] from baseline on the Clinical Dementia Rating. Secondary and exploratory endpoints included additional clinical, biomarker and imaging measures [including] cerebrospinal fluid tau biomarkers and tau positron emission tomography.

key_facts.fact: Biogen said the data give it confidence to advance diranersen into registrational development; the FDA granted the drug Fast Track designation for Alzheimer's in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are excited by these Phase 2 data, which give us the confidence to advance diranersen to registrational development. We look forward to engaging with regulators and the broader Alzheimer's disease community on next steps,' said Priya Singhal, M.D., M.P.H., Executive Vice President and Head of Development at Biogen... In 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted Fast Track designation to diranersen for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

stories.headline: Calif and Anthropic's Mythos Build First Public macOS Kernel Exploit on M5 Silicon, Bypassing MIE

key_facts.fact: Calif researchers, working with Anthropic's Mythos Preview, built a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit that bypasses Apple's Memory Integrity Enforcement (MIE) on M5 silicon — described as the first public exploit of its kind.
key_facts.excerpt: the first public macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on M5 silicon, surviving MIE... To the best of our knowledge, this is the first public macOS kernel exploit on MIE hardware.

key_facts.fact: The chain is a data-only local privilege escalation against macOS 26.4.1 that starts as an unprivileged user using only normal system calls and ends with a root shell.
key_facts.excerpt: The exploit is a data-only kernel local privilege escalation chain targeting macOS 26.4.1 (25E253). It starts from an unprivileged local user, uses only normal system calls, and ends with a root shell.

key_facts.fact: Calif says Apple spent roughly five years building MIE; its team built the exploit in five days, with bugs found on April 25 and a working exploit completed by May 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple spent five years building hardware and software to make memory corruption exploits dramatically harder. Our engineers, working together with Mythos Preview, built a working exploit in five days... Bruce Dang found the bugs on April 25th... by May 1st we had a working exploit.

key_facts.fact: Apple confirmed it is reviewing the 55-page report Calif delivered in person at Apple Park; CEO Thai Duong said the attack 'couldn't have been pulled off by Mythos alone'.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is currently reviewing the report from Calif to validate its findings... Calif's chief executive, Thai Dong, said that the attack 'couldn't have been pulled off by Mythos alone and leveraged the very human cybersecurity expertise of some of Calif's hackers.'

key_facts.excerpt: California-based robotics startup, Figure AI, has completed a 24-hour test of its humanoid robots that have been operating 24 hours without failure, extending the operation into a multi-day operation. The company's three humanoid robots, named Bob, Frank, and Gary, are operating without human control and have already sorted over 28,000 packages.

key_facts.fact: The robots detect barcodes, place packages on conveyor belts using onboard cameras and AI reasoning, and run on Helix-02, a system combining vision, touch sensing, proprioception and whole-body control.
key_facts.excerpt: The robots detect barcodes, place packages on conveyor belts using onboard cameras and AI reasoning, and use Helix-02, a system designed to combine vision, touch sensing, proprioception, and whole-body control.

key_facts.fact: When a robot gets stuck or hits an unfamiliar situation, the Helix-02 system can trigger an autonomous reset and resume work with zero human intervention; the run was livestreamed online.

stories.headline: Intel Begins Testing Production of Low-End Apple iPhone, iPad and Mac Chips on 18A-P

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported on May 14 that Apple has kicked off low-end/legacy iPhone, iPad and Mac processor production at Intel on the 18A-P series using Foveros packaging.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has kicked off low-end/legacy iPhone, iPad, and Mac processors at Intel on the 18A-P series (using Foveros packaging).

key_facts.fact: Kuo said the order mix is roughly 80% iPhone, mirroring Apple's end-device sales mix, and that Apple views Intel as 'one of the very few, and arguably the most complete' foundry training alternatives to TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: The order mix is roughly 80% iPhone, mirroring Apple's end-device sales mix... 'For the next several years, the bulk of advanced-node orders will remain with TSMC. Apple is therefore one of the very few, and arguably the most complete, foundry training opportunities available to' Intel.

key_facts.fact: Apple believes TSMC's resources will continue tilting toward AI customers, motivating the dual-source strategy with Intel's Arizona fabs.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple reportedly weighs Intel's 18A-P for 2027 entry-level Mac chips, challenging TSMC's exclusive grip... Apple's potential Intel partnership hinges on 18A-P process maturity by 2027.

key_facts.fact: Intel's 18A-P is the company's first node to support Foveros Direct 3D hybrid bonding, using a pitch of less than 5 microns to stack multiple chiplets through TSVs.
key_facts.excerpt: The 18A-P process is a derivative announced by Intel at the Direct Connect 2025, the company's first node to support Foveros Direct 3D hybrid bonding. stories.headline: Russia Pounds Kyiv With 670+ Drones and 56 Missiles, Killing at Least 24 in Largest Two-Day Aerial Assault of War

key_facts.fact: Russian overnight attack on May 14 killed at least 24 people, including two children, in Kyiv after 675 attack drones and 56 missiles were launched at Ukraine; air defenses downed 652 drones and 41 missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia pummeled Kyiv for hours on Thursday, May 14, firing hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles in an attack that killed at least 24 people, including two children... The Ukrainian air force said Russia had launched 675 attack drones and 56 missiles, mainly at Kyiv, adding its air defense units had downed 652 of the drones and 41 missiles.

key_facts.fact: Over Wednesday and Thursday combined, Russia launched 1,567 drones and at least 27 civilians were killed, the largest aerial barrage over a two-day window since the start of the invasion in 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia carried out its largest aerial attack over a two-day period since the start of its war in Ukraine, pounding the capital Kyiv and other cities with hundreds of drones... Russia had launched 1,567 drones since the start of Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. At least 27 civilians have been killed over the two days, officials said.

key_facts.fact: The attack came after a three-day US-brokered ceasefire expired late Monday and as Trump met Xi in Beijing; Ukrainian FM Andriy Sybiha said the strike showed Russia wanted to keep fighting despite Washington's peace push.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha noted that the attack had taken place during a crucial summit between US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping, and urged the two leaders to exert pressure on Russia. 'I am certain that the leaders of the United States and China have enough leverage over Moscow to tell Putin to finally end the war,' he said.

key_facts.fact: EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc is finalizing a €6 billion ($7B) drone support package for Ukraine and would keep tightening sanctions on Russia's war economy.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are finalising a €6 billion ($7bn; £5bn) drone support package. And we keep the pressure on Russia's war economy with ever tougher sanctions,' von der Leyen added.

key_facts.fact: Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu reiterated on May 14 that ending the war requires Ukraine to return to 'non-aligned, neutral and non-nuclear' status.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu has outlined conditions for ending the war in Ukraine... the Russian Security Council secretary stressed that Ukraine must return to 'non-aligned, neutral and non-nuclear principles.'

stories.headline: OPEC+ Plans Phased Quota Hikes Through September Even as Hormuz Blockage Drives Saudi Output to 36-Year Low

key_facts.fact: OPEC+ delegates said on May 14 the group aims to complete restoration of a 1.65 million bpd cut in three more monthly tranches through September, finishing on paper even though most members cannot actually deliver the barrels.
key_facts.excerpt: Key OPEC+ members aim to continue a series of oil quota increases over the next few months, completing the return of a layer of halted production — if only on paper — by the end of September, delegates said... The group already formally agreed to restore about two-thirds of a 1.65 million barrels a day supply cutback that it made back in 2023. It plans to raise targets further and revive the final portion in three more monthly stages.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia's output plunged to 6.3 million bpd in April, the lowest level since 1990, Kuwait is down to about a quarter of pre-war levels, and OPEC production has fallen ~9.7 million bpd (30%+) since the Iran war began Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC's secretariat body in Vienna that its output plunged even further in April to just 6.3 million barrels a day, marking the lowest level since 1990, the organization said in a monthly report on Wednesday. Kuwait's output is down to just a quarter of pre-war levels.

key_facts.fact: The IEA said global oil supply has lost 12.8 million bpd since the war started, with cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers exceeding one billion barrels and inventories falling at a record pace.
key_facts.excerpt: The oil market report for May noted that global oil supply declined by a further 1.8 million barrels per day in April, taking total losses to 12.8 mb/d since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28.

key_facts.fact: OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast to 1.17 million bpd from 1.38 million bpd previously, while the IEA forecasts demand will contract by 420,000 bpd this year.
key_facts.excerpt: World oil demand will rise by 1.17 million barrels per day in 2026, OPEC said, down from 1.38 million bpd expected previously. For 2027, OPEC expects oil demand to rise by 1.54 million bpd, up 200,000 bpd from the previous forecast.

key_facts.fact: The next OPEC+ policy meeting is set for June 7 to decide July output levels; remaining members already approved a modest 188,000 bpd increase for June, with the UAE having formally exited OPEC on May 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The United Arab Emirates recently quit OPEC due to internal friction over OPEC limits... The remaining OPEC members have ratified a modest increase of 188,000 barrels a daily for June.

stories.headline: TSMC Forecasts $1.5T Chip Market by 2030, Says AI Wafer Demand to Rise 11x by 2026

key_facts.fact: TSMC told its 2026 Technology Symposium on May 14 that AI accelerator wafer demand is projected to grow 11-fold between 2022 and 2026, and raised its global semiconductor market forecast to exceed $1.5 trillion by 2030, up from a previous $1 trillion estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC held its Taiwan Technology Symposium today. According to Reuters, the company said that demand for AI accelerator wafers is projected to grow 11-fold between 2022 and 2026. TSMC also raised its forecast for the global semiconductor market, now expecting it to exceed US$1.5 trillion by 2030, up from its previous US$1 trillion estimate.

key_facts.fact: Capacity for TSMC's 2nm and next-generation A16 nodes is projected to grow at a 70% CAGR from 2026 to 2028, while CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity is forecast to grow at more than 80% CAGR from 2022 to 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC said capacity for its most advanced 2nm and next-generation A16 chips is projected to grow at a 70% CAGR from 2026 to 2028, while CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate) advanced packaging capacity is forecast to achieve a CAGR of more than 80% from 2022 to 2027.

key_facts.fact: TSMC plans to build nine phases of wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities in 2026, and currently mass-produces a 5.5-reticle CoWoS at 98% yield, with plans for a 14-reticle, 20-HBM-stack version in 2028 and a 24-HBM-stack version in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also plans to build nine phases of wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities in 2026... TSMC's currently mass-produced 5.5-reticle-size version is the world's largest today and has already achieved yields of 98%. The report adds that TSMC plans to rapidly scale CoWoS, targeting a 14-reticle-size version capable of integrating 20 HBM stacks in 2028, before moving beyond 14 reticles with support for up to 24 HBM stacks in 2029.

key_facts.fact: TSMC said its Arizona output is expected to increase 1.8-fold year over year by 2026, with the first fab in production, tool move-in for fab 2 in 2H26, fab 3 under construction, and work on fab 4 and the site's first advanced-packaging facility set to begin this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Arizona: The first fab is already in production. Tool move-in for the second fab is planned for the second half of 2026. Construction of a third fab is underway. Work on a fourth fab and the site's first advanced packaging facility is expected to begin this year. TSMC anticipates a 1.8-fold year-on-year increase in Arizona output by 2026, with yields comparable to those in Taiwan.

key_facts.fact: AI and high-performance computing are expected to account for 55% of the $1.5 trillion market, followed by smartphones at 20% and automotive at 10%.
key_facts.excerpt: AI and high-performance computing are expected to account for 55 per cent of the $1.5 trillion market, followed by smartphones with 20 per cent, and automotive applications with 10 per cent, according to TSMC.

stories.headline: US Retail Sales Rise 0.5% and Jobless Claims Hit 211K as Iran-War Inflation Pressures Mount

key_facts.fact: US retail sales rose 0.5% in April after a downwardly revised 1.6% jump in March, the Commerce Department said on May 14; gasoline prices rose 12.3% in April amid the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: Retail sales rose 0.5% last month after a downwardly revised 1.6% jump in March, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Thursday... Gasoline prices rose 12.3% in April, data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration showed.

key_facts.fact: Initial jobless claims rose 12,000 to a seasonally adjusted 211,000 for the week ended May 9, above the 205,000 forecast; continuing claims climbed 24,000 to 1.782 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Initial claims for state unemployment benefits rose 12,000 to a seasonally adjusted 211,000 for the week ended May 9, the Labor Department said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 205,000 claims for the latest week... The number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 24,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.782 million during the week ended May 2.

key_facts.fact: US import prices jumped 1.9% in April, much more than expected; producer prices recorded their biggest monthly gain in over four years and consumer prices rose 3.8% YoY, the largest annual jump in three years.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Import Prices Jump 1.9% In April, Much More Than Expected... 05/14/2026 - 10:49 AM (RTTNews)(RTTNews) - The Labor Department released a report on Thursday showing a substantial increase in i...

key_facts.fact: Markets price little chance of any Fed rate cuts this year, with odds of a hike climbing to about 39% after the PPI report; the Fed has held its benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% as Iran-war inflation proves sticky.
key_facts.excerpt: Market pricing points to little chance of any interest rate cuts through the rest of the year, though odds for a hike climbed to about 39% following the PPI report. The Fed has kept its benchmark interest rate anchored in a range between 3.5%-3.75% as inflation has proved sticky and the labor market has been resilient.

key_facts.fact: Excluding gas, retail sales rose only 0.3% in April, with furniture and clothing stores slipping as higher gas costs eat into discretionary spending.
key_facts.excerpt: Excluding gas sales, retail sales in April were up 0.3%. That's a slowdown from the 0.7% pace, excluding business from gas stations, in March... Shoppers pulled back on spending in April as higher gas prices fueled by the Iran war meant less money left over for some nonessentials like clothing and furniture.
